results.name: Cable Face Pull With Rope
instructions: Set a cable pulley at upper chest height and attach a rope.
Hold the rope ends with an overhand grip and step back until your arms are straight.
Pull the rope toward your face, separating the ends and driving your elbows out and back.
Squeeze your shoulder blades, then return slowly and repeat.
tips: Keep your elbows high.
Finish with your hands beside your ears.
results.description: Cable Face Pull With Rope is a beginner multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Traps, Rotator Cuff.

results.name: Cable Front Raises Straight Bar
instructions: Attach a straight bar to a low pulley on a cable machine. Stand facing away from the machine, with your feet shoulder-width apart and the bar held with an overhand grip, palms facing down.
Stand upright with your back straight and core engaged. Let the bar hang down in front of your thighs with your arms fully extended and the cable passing between your legs.
Raise the bar in front of you to shoulder height, keeping your arms straight but with a slight bend in the elbows.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you raise the bar and inhale as you lower it back down.
Avoid using momentum; focus on the contraction of your shoulder muscles.
Ensure your shoulders stay down and relaxed, not shrugged up towards your ears.
results.description: Cable Front Raises Straight Bar is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Upper Back.

results.name: Cable Lateral Raises
instructions: Stand in the middle of a cable machine with the handles attached to the low pulleys on either side, with your feet shoulder-width apart. Hold the left handle with your right hand and the right handle with your left hand, with the cables crossing in front of you. Stand
Stand upright with your back straight. Let the handles hang down in front of your thighs with your arms fully extended.
Raise the handles out to your sides until your arms are parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Choose a weight that allows you to complete the exercise with proper form.
Exhale as you raise the handles and inhale as you lower them back down.
Avoid using momentum; focus on the contraction of your shoulder muscles.
results.description: Cable Lateral Raises is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Cable Leaning Lateral Raise
instructions: Attach a single handle to a low pulley on a cable machine. Stand next to the machine on your left side, holding the handle with your right hand. Lean away from the machine, using your left hand to hold onto the machine for support.
Position your feet together, with your outside foot slightly in front for better stability. Let the handle hang down at your side with your arm fully extended.
Raise the handle out to the side until your arm is parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbow.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch sides.
tips: Exhale as you raise the handle and inhale as you lower it back down.
Avoid using momentum; focus on the contraction of your shoulder muscles.
Lean away from the machine to increase the range of motion and target the shoulder muscles more effectively.
results.description: Cable Leaning Lateral Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.

results.name: Cable One Arm Front Raise
instructions: Attach a single handle to a low pulley on a cable machine. Stand facing away from the machine, holding the handle with your right hand, palm facing back. Step forward to create tension in the cable.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your back straight. Let your arm fully extend down by your side.
Raise the handle straight in front of you to shoulder height, keeping your arm straight but with a slight bend in the elbow.
Slowly lower the handle back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Avoid locking your elbow; keep a slight bend to reduce strain on your joints.
Exhale as you raise the handle and inhale as you lower it back down.
Avoid locking your elbow; keep a slight bend to reduce strain on your joints.
results.description: Cable One Arm Front Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Chest, Upper Back.

results.name: Cable Rear Delt Fly
instructions: Stand in the center of a cable machine with the pulleys set at chest height. Cross the cable ends and hold the left cable end with your right hand and the right cable end with your left hand, arms extended in front of you.
Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, keeping your back straight and a slight bend in your knees.
Pull the handles apart and out to the sides, keeping your arms straight but with a slight bend in the elbows, until your arms are extended out to your sides.
Slowly return to the starting position with control, bringing the handles back in front of you. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you pull the handles apart and inhale as you return to the starting position.
Use a lighter weight to ensure proper form and gradually increase the resistance as you get stronger.
Focus on engaging your rear deltoids and upper back during the movement.
results.description: Cable Rear Delt Fly is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Forearms.

results.name: Cable Rear Drive Bent Arm
instructions: Stand straight with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing the cable machine. Set the pulley at shoulder height and grasp the handle of the cable with your right hand, palm facing down. Set your arm parallel to the floor in front of you and bent at 90 degrees.
Drive your elbow sideways, keeping your arm bent at 90 degrees, pulling the cable across your chest.
Slowly bring your arm back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions, then switch to your left hand.
tips: Focus on squeezing your upper back muscles at the top of the movement.
Maintain a neutral wrist position to prevent strain.
Stand with a slight bend in your knees for better stability.
results.description: Cable Rear Drive Bent Arm is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the upper back (back). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Triceps, Upper Back, Shoulders.

results.name: Cable Reverse Fly on Crossover
instructions: Stand between two cable columns at shoulder height, and grasp the opposite cable handle in each hand with your arms crossed in front of your chest and a slight fixed bend in your elbows. Palms facing down (pronated grip).
Pull both handles outward and backward in a wide horizontal arc until your arms are straight to your side and your hands are aligned with your shoulders.
Pause briefly while squeezing your rear shoulders and upper back at the end of the movement.
Slowly return the handles along the same wide arc to the starting position and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your chest up and your spine in a neutral position.
Keep your shoulders down and avoid shrugging during the exercise.
Control the return phase to maintain constant muscle tension.
Inhale as you return to the starting position and exhale as you pull the handles apart.
results.description: Cable Reverse Fly on Crossover is a beginner single-joint isolation pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Middle Back, Shoulders, Forearms.

results.name: Cable Seated Rear Lateral Raise
instructions: Sit on the edge of a bench in the middle of a cable machine with the pulleys set at the lowest position. Attach single handles to each pulley and grasp the left handle with your right hand and the right handle with your left hand, allowing the cables to cross under your thighs.
Bend forward at the hips, keeping your back straight, so your chest is close to your knees.
Raise both handles out to the sides until your arms are parallel to the floor, keeping a slight bend in your elbows.
Slowly lower the handles back to the starting position with control. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Exhale as you raise the handles and inhale as you lower them back down.
Ensure your feet are firmly planted on the floor for stability.
Focus on engaging your rear deltoids and upper back during the movement.
results.description: Cable Seated Rear Lateral Raise is a beginner single-joint isolation pushing exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with a cable, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Forearms.

results.name: Cable Upright Row With EZ Bar
instructions: Stand with your feet shoulder-width apart, facing the cable machine with an EZ bar attached to the low pulley. Grasp the EZ bar with both hands using an overhand grip (palms facing down), hands shoulder-width apart.
Pull the EZ bar upwards towards your chin by bending your elbows and raising your upper arms, leading with your elbows, keeping the bar close to your body.
Slowly lower the bar back to the starting position with control.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Keep your back straight and avoid using momentum.
Keep your elbows higher than your wrists throughout the movement.
Exhale as you pull the EZ bar up and inhale as you lower it back down.
results.description: Cable Upright Row With EZ Bar is an intermediate multi-joint compound pulling exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with an ez barbell, it falls under the strength category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back.
